comment: Still a bargain. Nearly every song ever made, offline downloads, no ads, for about 13 bucks a month is massively undervalued. It's roughly a CD album a month for basically my whole listening life, and I pay the artists. Worth it for me, even after two bumps.

Cool, the price goes up and the artists still get pennies for their streams. Meanwhile the CEO keeps his billions. I buy music directly when I can, and this just makes me think harder about paying the money vacuum at all.

Another bump, sure. I don't really think about price, I need the library for transcribing other people's songs anyway. Discover Weekly is still recycling the same top 40 and I still can't turn off Made For You, but my playlists are here, so I'm not going anywhere.

Price goes up again and playback still breaks every other day, wtf. Lossless does sound great on my speakers, but if the queue bugs and the Mix thing keep going I'm moving to Apple Music, no question.

Great, another price increase, and I still don't have a straight answer on my billing. I'm on a multi-month block so I'm covered for now, but if I get charged after cancelling again I'm going straight to support and posting every step. The copy-paste reply is not an answer.

Yeah it's annoying but still a steal. $12.99 for music, podcasts and audiobooks in one app, and the family plan is still cheap per person. Not going to bother switching for a couple bucks, it's worth every penny to me.

Another increase and the recommendations are still just the same stuff on repeat. I've got YouTube Premium already, which comes with a music player, so this makes less and less sense. Staying for Jam for now but I'm honestly one bad month from just using YouTube Music.
Price is up again, but on Duo with my wife it's still fine for us. Discover Weekly is my Monday thing and the new features are finally showing up. Not thrilled but not leaving either.

Premium going up again while the app won't even play the next song. Amazon Music is cheaper and has playlists Spotify is missing anyway. I already cancelled once, I'm just moving over. contacted support, got nothing.
Price goes up and the artists still get nothing, and the AI slop is still in my Discover Weekly. I already left once. Not paying more to get fake artists shoved in my face, screw this.

same issue here, the bug is still there after reinstalling everything. Price going up on a service that won't even play music right is just lol. If it's not fixed by the next bill I'm out, probably to YouTube Music.

Cancelled already so the price bump doesn't touch me, lol. Glad I moved to Apple Music, because Discover Weekly was just AI slop and the same songs in rotation. Spotify can keep raising prices for the people still paying.

Student went from 5.99 to 6.99, which still hurts a bit on a student budget. But it's way better than full price. Please let my Hulu stay bundled when I re-verify, that's the part I'm actually worried about.

Spotify just got more expensive again and Apple Music is still cheaper with better sound. I keep saying I'm going to switch, but my family playlists and the friend playlists are a pain to rebuild, so I'm stuck with Spotify for now.

Another price rise, and the lossless and AI playlist stuff is still locked out based on where we live. We pay the same as everybody else and get fewer features. The household plan is still worth its weight in gold for my parents, but this is getting unfair.
Don't care about the price bump. Nobody can hear lossless over Bluetooth anyway, 320 is fine. Not paying extra for a placebo, and I'm not leaving over it.

Price went up again, meh. Search and multi-device sync are still the reason I'm here, and rebuilding years of playlists somewhere else would be a nightmare. If they change something I really hate I'll stop the subscription, but this one doesn't bother me.
Still worth it for me. Ad-free, skipping whatever I want, uploading my own stuff, and it's still cheaper than buying the albums. Yeah it's pricey but no complaints here, been paying since forever.

Price goes up again, fine, whatever. What actually bugs me is the New Episodes folder is gone and episodes still play in reverse. If the podcast side doesn't get fixed I'm moving to Apple Podcasts, honestly the stupidest update yet.
I pay for Premium and they're still jamming unskippable ads into my podcasts? Raising the price on top of that is a joke. One more ad and I'm deleting my account, I'm done.
Price goes up again and shuffle still sucks, same 10-15 songs over and over. Free shuffle honestly works better than Premium shuffle for me. I'm seriously thinking about dropping back to free.

Another price increase while features keep disappearing without any explanation. Crossfade is still here but barely, and the app keeps getting more bloated with ads. If they keep stripping stuff I'm gone.
Family goes up to 21.99. Still the cheapest way to cover my household, and split six ways it's fine. Annoyed about the address lockouts and no lossless, but I'm not dropping it over a price bump.
Price up and the discography is still a PITA to find. Feels like we're paying more for worse every time. Family plan keeps me here for now but the artist pages still being broken is not okay.
Premium is up to 12 now? lol no. Free Spotify is still ass with the skip limits, but I'm not paying that for a few songs. I'd just buy YouTube Premium before I gave Spotify another dime.
Premium going up again and I'm supposed to be excited? Why do I have to pay for features that should come with the free app. Still sick of the ads and skip limits. Ridiculous at this point.

Price goes up and lossless still isn't really true lossless on my setup. Cheaper services already do it right. I'm staying for the recommendations for now, but Tidal is looking better every time they raise prices.

Premium up again? I'm already on free for a reason. Playlists still play random songs instead of the ones I picked, and I've switched to Apple Music before. Is anyone else seeing this or is it just me?
